blog_summary: Adrian Colyer revisits Rumelhart et al.'s seminal 1986 paper on back-propagation, highlighting its role as a breakthrough algorithm for training neural networks with hidden layers. The blog post emphasizes how back-propagation enables hidden units to learn meaningful representations of input data by adjusting weights through gradient descent. Colyer walks through the paper's explanation of feed-forward computation, error calculation, and the chain rule-based derivation of weight updates, noting the elegance of the approach despite its simplicity. He also points out the paper's foundational contributions to modern deep learning, including the introduction of skip connections and momentum-based optimization techniques.
